stem: Using the Mend & Move Refill Co. stimulus, describe one difference between profit and cash, and apply this difference to the business.

points.descriptor: Identifies profit as revenue less relevant costs over a period.
accept: Profit is the amount remaining after relevant costs are deducted from revenue.
Profit measures financial performance over a period.

points.descriptor: Identifies cash as money held or cash received and paid by the business, rather than profit.
accept: Cash is the money available to make payments.
Cash is affected by the timing of receipts and payments.
Profit and cash are not the same.

points.descriptor: Applies the distinction to Mend & Move using relevant stimulus evidence.
accept: Mend & Move made £150,000 profit in 2026 but held only £85,000 cash at the year end.
Its cash was reduced by buying refill sachets in advance and paying for delivery crates, despite making a profit.
The business may make a profit but still need sufficient cash to pay suppliers on time.

mark_scheme.model_answer: Profit is the amount left after relevant costs are deducted from revenue over a period, whereas cash is the money available to make payments. Mend & Move made a £150,000 profit in 2026 but held £85,000 cash because advance purchases of sachets and delivery crates reduced its cash balance.
